analysis:
Reviewed the new ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift and the ProviderLoop+Serve.swift shutdown changes.

Recovery is a provider-local residency scheduler that runs on the capacity tick. It loads selected models without evicting (allowEviction: false) and unloads only unselected, idle, unprotected models. Each victim is rechecked right before unload via selectedModelRecoveryMayStillEvict and the pause-reason guard. The code touches no prompt data (A-001), keys, attestation or authorization (T-052/T-053), and no coordinator wire messages. I saw no change to the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041). One unverified detail: unloading a model may trigger cache or KV cleanup, and unloadModel(forEviction:) is not supplied, so its cache-purge behavior is unchecked.

The availability edge looks bounded. Pruning, the pause reasons (draining, Autopilot lease, model switch, preload) and the in-progress attempt guard prevent concurrent residency changes. Attempt ownership is set only after the post-await recheck. Backoff limits retry churn. The report exposes only model IDs and blocker text in the daemon state file. Those IDs are already public via heartbeats and advertisements, so I treated this as no meaningful new disclosure.

In Serve.swift (lines 486 and 512), the recovery task is added to the preload cancel-and-wait list at shutdown. This is a hardening change that stops recovery from racing teardown. The inline unload loop is replaced by unloadAllModelsForShutdown(), whose definition is not supplied. The next pass should confirm it preserves the base semantics: wait for in-flight unloads and loop until modelSlots is empty, so decrypted KV and GPU residue (T-028) is not left behind or hung on. Also confirm that a recovery task that outlives the 'waitForPreloads' timeout cannot reload a model after the unload sweep. isShuttingDown is set earlier, and the attempt checks it before load, which mitigates that. The ensureModelLoaded(allowEviction:false) and selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride internals are unverified.

No concrete regression identified.
